questions.stem: Which of the following points lies on the line y = 3x - 5?
questions.explanation: Substitute each point: (1, -2): y = 3(1) - 5 = -2. This matches. (2, -1): y = 3(2) - 5 = 1, not -1. (3, 5): y = 3(3) - 5 = 4, not 5.

questions.stem: The line y = 2x + 1 crosses the x-axis at which point?
questions.explanation: At the x-axis, y = 0. Set 0 = 2x + 1. 2x = -1. x = -0.5. The crossing point is (-0.5, 0).

questions.stem: Which equation represents a horizontal line passing through (3, -4)?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line has the same y-value everywhere. Since it passes through (3, -4), the equation is y = -4. (x = 3 would be a vertical line.)

questions.stem: When y = -x + 6 is plotted, which statement is true?

options.text: The line slopes upward and crosses the y-axis at 6
The line slopes downward and crosses the y-axis at 6
The line slopes downward and crosses the y-axis at -6
The line is horizontal at y = 6

questions.explanation: In y = mx + c form: m = -1 (negative gradient, so slopes downward) and c = 6 (y-intercept at 6).

questions.stem: The lines y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x - 1 are plotted on the same axes. What is true about them?
questions.explanation: Both have gradient m = 2, but different y-intercepts (3 and -1). Lines with the same gradient are parallel and never intersect.
